# AuthRight Harness

> Identity & Access Security Decision Layer for AI coding agents.

AuthRight Harness is the decision layer between your codebase and implementation. Two surfaces share that layer. The CLI plus Cursor, Codex, or Claude Code runs the full loop. [AuthRight Studio](/studio-docs) is the local browser host: auto-plan Decide and an IAM source-of-truth document. Studio does not run explore, doctor, request-match, to-openspec, or to-plan.

## Documentation

Two help sets. Installation and the product intro appear in both, in reading order. Releases is a separate site page. Studio help does not include OpenSpec, Agent Plan, or the CLI command reference.

- [Choose a help set](/docs)
- [CLI help](/cli-docs) — first loop, then handoff and reference
- [Studio help](/studio-docs) — principles, workflow, Cases, models, proxy
- [Installation](/cli-docs/installation) — `@authright/cli`, `@authright/studio`, or both
- [Releases](/releases) — shared version history for CLI and Studio

CLI, in order:

- [Existing projects](/cli-docs/existing-projects) · [Workflows](/cli-docs/workflows) · [Examples](/cli-docs/examples)
- Handoff: [Reviewing decisions](/cli-docs/reviewing-decisions) · [Implementation](/cli-docs/impl) · [OpenSpec](/cli-docs/openspec) · [Agent Plan-mode](/cli-docs/agent-plan)
- Lookup: [How commands work](/cli-docs/how-commands-work) · [Commands](/cli-docs/commands) · [CLI](/cli-docs/cli) · [Agents](/cli-docs/agents)
- [Overview](/cli-docs/overview)
- [IAM Ontology](/ontology) — interactive graph of the shipped concept model
- [FAQ](/cli-docs/faq)

## Quick start

```bash
npm install -g @authright/cli@latest
cd your-project && authright init
# Studio-only, no CLI required:
npm install -g @authright/studio@latest
authright-studio
```

Public loop: `scan` → pick `explore` or `change` → on that Auth Change record: `--analyze` → (explore: Agenda HITL | change: plan → `--set` → `--confirm-plan`) → `--ready` → `request-match` → `to-openspec` | `to-plan` → `review`. `doctor` is a peer command: it reads **application source** and writes a clear risk report at `.authright/diagnosis/report.md` (it does not redesign identity). You can run it before explore or change. `/auth:doc` is different—it writes a summary of **decisions** under `.authright/docs/`.

`/auth:explore` and `/auth:change` are two Decide commands — pick one. Explore is interactive recommend-and-choose; change is auto-plan. `/auth:to-openspec` and `/auth:to-plan` are two handoff commands — pick one. Product intent names use colon form (`/auth:scan`, `/auth:explore`, `/auth:change`, `/auth:request-match`, `/auth:to-openspec`, `/auth:to-plan`, `/auth:review`, `/auth:doc`, `/auth:doctor`). Cursor registers hyphen slashes from the filename (`/auth-scan`); Claude Code registers colon slashes from `.claude/commands/auth/` (`/auth:scan`); Codex skills use `$authright-scan`. `authright init` prints the installed hosts’ forms.

AuthRight Harness does not write application source. It prepares accepted identity-security decisions for OpenSpec or Agent Plan-mode handoff (pick one).
